findings.claim: Eduqas Theme 6 starts with this puzzle
findings.truth: House rule: an Eduqas/WJEC lesson must never name the board in student-facing prose. Neutral wording: 'Theme 6 starts with this puzzle'.
findings.evidence: house rule in CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md

findings.claim: The UK's GDP per capita in 2024 sat at around US$48,000 ... the United States at about US$80,000
findings.truth: World Bank 2025 GDP per capita: UK US$57,602, USA US$90,027, Bangladesh US$2,597. The UK and US figures are 15-20 per cent too low; the Bangladesh figure is right.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, List of countries by GDP (nominal) per capita, World Bank (2025) column

findings.claim: Gross National Income (GNI) - the headline measure used by Eduqas - is broader than GDP
findings.truth: Names the board (house rule). The spec treats GNI and GDP as alternatives ('for example, GNI, GDP'), so 'the headline measure in this topic' is both neutral and accurate.
findings.evidence: spec Key Idea 6.1.1; house rule

findings.claim: China's GDP (about US$18 trillion in 2024) is roughly six times the UK's - but China has 21 times more people ... UK GDP per capita is about US$48,000 versus China's US$13,000
findings.truth: Recomputed from World Bank 2025 per-capita values: China about US$19tn, UK about US$4.0tn, a ratio near five, not six. Population ratio is 20, not 21. Per-capita figures are US$58,000 and US$14,000.
findings.evidence: recomputation from Wikipedia/World Bank 2025 per-capita values

findings.claim: Both stories are true, and Eduqas examiners want students who can see both at once.
findings.truth: Names the board and invents an examiner preference. Neutral: 'a strong answer shows both at once'.
findings.evidence: house rule; no published examiner statement supports the claim

findings.claim: For 4-mark compare questions, examiners want explicit linking words
findings.truth: Invented examiner claim. Give the advice directly: 'use explicit linking words'.
findings.evidence: no published examiner statement supports the claim

findings.claim: EU sugar subsidies, for example, made it cheaper for African producers to sell cane sugar to Europe than for Europeans to buy it - until the subsidies were reformed.
findings.truth: The sentence is garbled and states the effect backwards. EU sugar subsidies made European beet sugar artificially cheap, so African cane growers struggled to compete, until the regime was reformed.
findings.evidence: spec 6.2.1 (consequences of protectionist policies including subsidies); standard account of the EU sugar regime

findings.claim: its iPhones are assembled in China and Vietnam
findings.truth: iPhone final assembly happens in China and India (Foxconn, Wistron, Tata). Vietnam builds other Apple products, not iPhones.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, iPhone - manufacturing section

findings.claim: Around 60% of Zambia's export earnings still come from copper.
findings.truth: Copper is well over 70 per cent of Zambian export earnings (Wikipedia's Economy of Zambia gives 85 per cent; World Bank commentary gives over 70 per cent). 'More than 70%' is safe under both.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Economy of Zambia

findings.claim: A trade bloc lowers air-fare taxes, so tourists fly to Kenya instead of holidaying at home.
findings.truth: Trade blocs cut tariffs on goods; they do not set air-fare taxes. The real drivers named in the spec are changing technology and communications, so cheaper flights and online booking.
findings.evidence: spec 6.2.1(b) - causes and key drivers of a globalised tourist industry

findings.claim: How trade rules, multinationals and tourism create uneven development between richer and poorer countries.
findings.truth: 106 characters; the validator limit is under 100. Trimming 'richer and poorer' keeps the meaning.
findings.evidence: validator limit in CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md

findings.claim: markers want to see 'On balance...'
findings.truth: Invented examiner claim. Give the advice directly: 'write On balance...'.
findings.evidence: no published examiner statement supports the claim

findings.claim: Fairtrade-certified cocoa farmers in Ghana receive at least US$2,400 per tonne, plus an extra premium of US$240 per tonne
findings.truth: These are the values Fairtrade International set in 2019. Fairtrade announced an increase (understood to be US$2,600 per tonne minimum price and US$300 per tonne premium) taking effect on 1 January 2025, but fairtrade.net returned 404/redirect loops this session and no permitted source could confirm it. Options: (a) update to US$2,600 / US$300 once the Fairtrade price table is read; (b) leave as is until confirmed. Recommend (a) - check the price table, then update the content sentence and flashcard [9] together.
findings.evidence: fairtrade.net unreachable; Wikipedia Fairtrade certification carries no figures

findings.claim: The UK transfers water from rainy upland Wales (Lake Vyrnwy) to the much drier Midlands.
findings.truth: Lake Vyrnwy supplies Merseyside, not the Midlands. The Wales-to-Midlands transfer is the Elan Valley reservoirs to Birmingham, carried by gravity through a 73-mile (117 km) aqueduct to Frankley.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Elan Valley Reservoirs

findings.claim: The Akosombo Dam ... irrigates farmland across the south of the country
findings.truth: Akosombo's primary purpose was electricity for the aluminium industry. Irrigation is not among its functions.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Akosombo Dam

findings.claim: markers want a clear 'On balance...' statement
findings.truth: Invented examiner claim. Give the advice directly.
findings.evidence: no published examiner statement supports the claim

findings.claim: Global water consumption has more than doubled since 1980.
findings.truth: This looks overstated. The UN's published line is that global water use has grown about six-fold over the past hundred years and continues to rise by roughly 1 per cent a year, which since 1980 is a rise of about a half, not a doubling. UN Water and UNESCO pages returned 403/no figures this session and no permitted source could confirm a replacement. Recommend replacing 'has more than doubled since 1980' with 'has grown six-fold over the last hundred years and still rises by about 1% a year' once the UN World Water Development Report figure is read.
findings.evidence: unwater.org 403; UNESCO release and Wikipedia carry no growth figure

findings.claim: farmers have pumped so heavily that water tables are falling several metres a year
findings.truth: Published decline rates for north-west India and the US south-west are generally under a metre a year, with local exceptions. Not corrected: no permitted source reached this session.
findings.evidence: not verified

findings.claim: London still loses around a fifth of its supply to leaks
findings.truth: Thames Water leakage runs nearer a quarter of supply. The claim is in the right region and no exact figure was verified.
findings.evidence: not verified

findings.claim: Boys born in Blackpool today have a life expectancy nearly nine years lower than boys born in parts of west London.
findings.truth: ONS: male life expectancy was lowest in Blackpool (73.4 years) and highest in Hart (83.7 years), a gap of 10.3 years - 'more than a decade'. Both the size of the gap and the named comparison area are wrong.
findings.evidence: ONS, Life expectancy for local areas of the UK, 2020 to 2022

findings.claim: Average GDP per person in inner London is more than double the figure for the north-east of England.
findings.truth: True but vague, and 'inner London' understates the gap badly (Inner London West is several times the North East). ONS 2023: London GDP per head 69,077 pounds, North East 28,583 pounds - a usable, quotable pair.
findings.evidence: ONS, Regional economic activity by gross domestic product, UK, 1998 to 2023

findings.claim: HS2, the proposed high-speed line from London to Birmingham (and originally to Manchester and Leeds) ... Northern Powerhouse Rail and Crossrail upgrades aim to do the same.
findings.truth: HS2 Phase 1 is under construction, not proposed; the Leeds leg went in the 2021 Integrated Rail Plan and the Manchester leg was cancelled in October 2023. Crossrail is a London scheme and does not rebalance towards the north - the Transpennine Route Upgrade does.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, High Speed 2; spec 6.4.3 names HS2 as the major-infrastructure example

findings.claim: markers want to see 'On balance, infrastructure helps but only if combined with skills and devolution.'
findings.truth: Invented examiner claim. Give the advice directly.
findings.evidence: no published examiner statement supports the claim

findings.claim: Cuba's GNI per capita is only US$9,500 but Cubans live to 79 on average
findings.truth: Cuban life expectancy is nearer 78 and World Bank income data for Cuba is sparse and dated. Not corrected: no permitted source carried a current pair of figures.
findings.evidence: not verified

findings.claim: Norway ... 0.97; the UK at 0.94; India at 0.64; South Sudan ... 0.39
findings.truth: Mixed vintage: India 0.64 is the 2022 HDR value and the 2023 value is about 0.685. The other three are close to the latest report. Not corrected: the HDR was not reachable from a permitted source.
findings.evidence: not verified

findings.claim: Award up to 2 marks for a developed description
findings.truth: Four mark schemes in this lesson open with 'Award up to N marks for'. That is close to the banned rubric phrase 'Award N marks for' and may trip the copyright-distancing validator. Left alone: it is pre-existing and is not a fact error.
findings.evidence: banned-string list in CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md

findings.claim: the 2013 collapse of the Rana Plaza garment factory in Dhaka, which killed over 1,100 workers
findings.truth: The death toll is right. Rana Plaza stood in Savar in Greater Dhaka, and was a commercial building housing several garment factories rather than one factory.
findings.evidence: widely published account

summary: Five lessons checked against Core Theme 6 of the spec. Nineteen fixes: three board-naming breaches of the house rule, three wrong or garbled named examples (the EU sugar-subsidy sentence, Lake Vyrnwy for the Elan Valley, Akosombo irrigation), a wrong ONS life-expectancy gap, stale UK and US GDP-per-capita figures carried through content, flashcards and mark schemes, an out-of-date HS2 description, and four invented examiner claims. Two items need a ruling: the Fairtrade cocoa minimum price and the claim that global water use has more than doubled since 1980, neither confirmable from a reachable source this session.
